newsitem.title: UK: UK rejoins Euro military transport aircraft group.
newsitem.headline: UK rejoins Euro military transport aircraft group.

text.p: Britain announced on Thursday it was rejoining a pan-European project to build a new military transport plane, the Future Large Aircraft (FLA).

Defence Secretary George Robertson said in a parliamentary written answer Britain had decided to join at least five other European governments in inviting the Airbus Industrie consortium's new military arm to bid to develop and build the new aircraft.
The FLA project could be worth over $22 billion to the Airbus Military partners if their European governments decide to go ahead and order the aircraft.
"I have now decided that the UK should rejoin our European partners in issuing a Request for Proposals to Airbus Military Company for the Future Large Aircraft," Robertson said in a statement.

He emphasised Britain would only go ahead with the project if the Airbus bid gave "value for money" and he invited other participating governments to seek rival bids from other aircraft manufacturers.
But he was confident Airbus would come up with acceptable proposals. "It looks as though the FLA is going to fly," he told reporters.

"I am confident that Airbus, which competes everyday of the week with Boeing and with the other large aerospace suppliers (in the commercial aircraft market) and competes very successfully, can confidently compete in this area as well," he said.

Robertson told a news conference Britain was looking at a target price of around $75 million an aircraft, with Britain seeking up to 40 or 50 aircraft "over a fairly lengthy period of time", which would be part of a pan-European order for nearer 300 aircraft.
The FLA project was designed by the European aircraft industry to challenge U.S. firm Lockheed Martin's dominance of the market for tactical transport aircraft.
It has been stuck on the drawing board for years due to lack of funding from sponsor governments but they got together at the Paris Airshow last month to revive the project as a commercial venture.

Lack of development funds from member governments has compelled the pan-European consortium to treat the project like a commercial aircraft project, to be managed by Airbus, with funding to be based on launch orders.

France, Germany, Italy, Spain and Turkey all gave their immediate go-ahead at the Paris meeting to making an official Request for Proposal (RFP), while Airbus said Britain was expected to join once the new Labour government had had time to consider the project.
Belgium and Portugal are also considering joining and Airbus said that it would be preparing its bid on the basis of the eight countries ordering around 291 aircraft.

A senior Ministry of Defence official confirmed on Thursday other aircraft being considered by Britain included the C130J, the new version of the Lockheed Martin's Hercules, and the giant C17 strategic airlifter made by Boeing's new subsidiary McDonnell Douglas.

Britain's previous Conservative government awarded Lockheed a billion pound order in 1994 for 25 new C130Js but said it would consider the FLA to replace the balance of its old Hercules fleet if the project was commercial, the price was right and it was available in time.

Members of the FLA industrial consortium include Airbus partners Aerospatiale of France, Daimler-Benz AG unit Daimler-Benz Aerospace (Dasa), British Aerospace Plc, and Spain's Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA), as well as Finmeccanica of Italy's Alenia unit.
